proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is closer to 1 week (or varies over time), the fixed 2-week delay can shift the peak and degrade short-horizon timing in validation.
proposals.rationale: Anchor candidate per prior feedback: SEIRS with a 2-week observation lag to reflect admissions lagging infections while keeping dynamics simple (non-fractional) for stability with 31 training weeks.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the earlier validation sensitivity was driven by boundary effects rather than fractional flexibility, this may still show split-dependent performance (especially near end-of-train).
proposals.rationale: Direct test of whether the previously best delay=1 can be stabilized by turning fractional dynamics off, isolating delay choice from added flexibility.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-lagging can smear/late-shift the inferred infection proxy, leading to underprediction around the rise and delayed peak relative to observed hospitalizations.
proposals.rationale: Robustness check one step beyond 2 weeks to cover plausible longer admission/reporting lags without changing structure family or adding complexity.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions lag infections materially, delay=0 will tend to predict peaks too early and may misrepresent the ascent/decline symmetry.
proposals.rationale: No-lag comparator to test whether the series behaves like a near-contemporaneous proxy of I despite hospitalization semantics; helps diagnose whether delay is truly identifiable in this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May overfit short training windows and exhibit poorer extrapolation/validation instability (regime-shift sensitivity), repeating the over-flexibility risk noted previously.
proposals.rationale: Controlled reintroduction of fractional dynamics at the anchored delay=2 to see if added flexibility helps capture moderate peakiness at high rate scale without changing observation mapping.
